stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $X$ be a ringed space. Let $j : U \to X$ be the
inclusion of an open. The $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $j_!\mathcal{O}_U$ is a
compact object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ if there exists an integer $d$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H^p(U, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for all $p > d$, and
\item the functors $\mathcal{F} \mapsto H^p(U, \mathcal{F})$
commute with direct sums.
\end{enumerate}
 The cohomological conditions are read as ranging over sheaves of modules on $U$ and the appropriate integers $p$; the original source suppresses the coefficient-class quantifier.
hypotheses: $X$ is a ringed space and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ is an open immersion.

There exists an integer $d$ with $H^p(U,\mathcal F)=0$ for all $p>d$ and the cohomology functors $\mathcal F\mapsto H^p(U,\mathcal F)$ commute with direct sums (for the relevant sheaf-module coefficients, and every $p$).

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $X$ be a ringed space. Assume that the underlying topological space
of $X$ has the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is quasi-compact,
\item there exists a basis of quasi-compact open subsets, and
\item the intersection of any two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact.
\end{enumerate}
Let $K$ be a perfect object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $K$ is a compact object of $D^+(\mathcal{O}_X)$
in the following sense: if $M = \bigoplus_{i \in I} M_i$ is
bounded below, then $\Hom(K, M) = \bigoplus_{i \in I} \Hom(K, M_i)$.
\item[(b)] If $X$ has finite cohomological dimension, i.e., if there exists
a $d$ such that $H^i(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for $i > d$, then
$K$ is a compact object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: $X$ is a ringed space whose underlying topological space is quasi-compact, has a basis of quasi-compact opens, and has quasi-compact intersections of any two quasi-compact opens.
$K$ is a perfect object of $D(\mathcal O_X)$.
conclusions: For any family $(M_i)$ in $D^+(\mathcal O_X)$ whose direct sum $M=\bigoplus_iM_i$ is bounded below, $\operatorname{Hom}(K,M)\simeq\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(K,M_i)$.
If, in addition, $X$ has finite cohomological dimension, then $K$ is compact in all of $D(\mathcal O_X)$.

reason: Compactness argument uses duality and derived global-sections commuting with sums, but the final display repeats a direct sum inside Γ and inherits the prior compactness lemma's concern.
